reasoning: The skill states that a shown result closes the work and the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery: once the verifier confirms the observable outcome, the Director shows the result and closes the checkpoint in the same step. Here the observable outcome named by the instruction — the eleven queue titles reading as plain sentences — is confirmed by artifacts that did not come from the executor's self-report: plan_checks.py exits 0 and names each rewritten row, and the regenerated board page shows the new titles. That is a buildable result a command and a plain read already confirm was delivered, which is exactly what rule 12/27 excludes from the three cases reserved for him. It is not a taste call, because no judgment of his is being solicited and no wording was contested; not a trade-off no artifact settles, since the checks and the page settle it; not a change to the definition of correct; and not irreversible, since the edit lives in git. His being asleep is irrelevant — leaving the row open to wait for him to look and bless what was already shown is the precise failure the rule forbids. So the Director clears IN PROGRESS and NEXT, runs checkpoint.py close on this work's existing checkpoint, and reports in one sentence what changed: PLAN.md's eleven titles, with before/now/added lines for the document. If he disagrees with the wording afterward, that is a new fact and becomes its own task carrying his correction; the closed row stays closed.
